column1: What is the primary articulation primitive in Bionicle construction, and what rotational freedom does it provide compared to standard Technic pin connections?
column2: The ball-and-socket joint, which provides three rotational degrees of freedom (spherical joint), versus a Technic pin connection which is a revolute joint restricted to one rotational axis and overconstrained in all others.

column1: What are the approximate dimensions of the original Mata ball-and-socket joint (socket entrance diameter and ball diameter)?
column2: The hemispherical socket cup entrance diameter is approximately 9.5 mm, and the Technic ball joint element is a 10 mm diameter sphere mounted on a stub axle.

column1: Mechanically, how does a Bionicle ball-and-socket joint generate retention force to hold a pose?
column2: The ABS socket walls elastically expand by roughly 0.25–0.35 mm as the ball is pressed in, creating a radial interference fit; a retention lip creates an undercut that produces a mechanical snap-lock once the ball's equator passes it, generating holding torque (~0.08–0.15 N·m fresh) via friction and normal force.

column1: Why does Bionicle joint holding torque degrade over time, and what is the practical implication for display models?
column2: Repeated articulation cycles cause microscopic wear at high-stress contact points on the ball and socket surfaces, reducing friction/interference-based holding torque; builders must account for this when designing models meant to maintain poses long-term.

column1: What is the 'ball-joint hierarchy' invariant in Bionicle part taxonomy?
column2: The principle that Bionicle uses a continuous chain of ball sockets and cups (resolving force in 3D simultaneously) rather than Technic's rigid pin-and-beam linkages, making every limb segment both a structural member and a posable kinematic link at once.

column1: Describe the 'shell-and-frame duality' invariant and its most common failure mode.
column2: Bionicle figures separate structural frame parts (which carry load, torque, and kinematic attachment points) from decorative armor shells (which clip/pin over the frame for visual mass and color). The common failure mode is treating shells as structural or expecting frames to carry visual weight alone.

column1: What is meant by 'generation-specific compatibility' in Bionicle parts, and why does it matter?
column2: Each design generation (e.g., Mata, Metru, Inika/Glatorian, 2015 reboot) introduced new socket sizes, pin geometries, and shell attachment conventions that only partially overlap across generations, so treating the entire part library as flat/interchangeable causes seemingly arbitrary incompatibilities.

column1: What is the first invariant of Bionicle biomechanical design theory regarding the skeleton?
column2: 'The skeleton is the form' — the skeletal framework is not hidden scaffolding but the primary load-bearing and articulation system, exposed and celebrated, with visual mass coming from structural members themselves (e.g., CCBS shells complete rather than merely cover the bone structure).

column1: How does Bionicle design theory treat bilateral symmetry, and why do asymmetric features carry visual weight?
column2: Bilateral symmetry (left mirrors right) is the default organizational heuristic—build one side, verify it, then mirror it. Deliberate asymmetries (e.g., a single oversized claw or shoulder cannon) read as intentional precisely because the symmetric baseline exists; without that baseline, asymmetry reads as incomplete or broken.

column1: What design trade-off exists between maximum posability and static display stability in Bionicle figures?
column2: A figure engineered with joints loose enough for maximum posability will sag over time under gravity/friction creep, meaning practitioners must choose between high posability and long-term pose retention rather than assuming both are free.

column1: What is a 'narrative silhouette' in Bionicle design, and give an example.
column2: The idea that a figure's visual profile, color distribution, part geometry, and articulation count encode narrative/character information. Example: Tahu Mata's heavy, shoulder-dominant frame and flame-colored Hau mask communicate aggression and leadership before any story is read.

column1: What is the fundamental torque relationship used in Bionicle joint holding-torque measurement, and what does each variable represent?
column2: τ = F × r, where τ is rotational moment (torque), F is the applied force, and r is the lever arm (moment arm) distance from the pivot point.
